points.description: States that data members can be accessed from any member function of the class (class-wide scope), not just from one function. Accept equivalent wording such as 'all member functions can use them' or 'accessible throughout the class'. No marks if the answer says a data member can only be accessed inside one member function.

States that a local variable can only be accessed inside the member function in which it is declared/defined (function-local scope). Accept equivalent wording such as 'only that function can use it' or 'not accessible from other member functions'. No marks if the answer says a local variable is accessible throughout the class.

Contrasts where they are declared: data members are declared in the class definition, whereas local variables are declared inside the member function that defines/uses them. Accept equivalent wording.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both the class-wide accessibility of data members and the function-local accessibility of local variables, plus the contrast in where they are declared. Award the relevant point(s) for each correct side; an answer that describes only one side earns only those points. No marks for saying data members are local to a function or local variables are accessible throughout the class.
